summary.headline: Softtech Q4 FY26 revenue rose 50% YoY to INR 46.6 crore and FY26 revenue hit INR 132.9 crore, with management targeting INR 300 crore by FY29.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 46.6 crore (up 50% YoY) with EBITDA margin of 21% versus 15% a year earlier, and PAT of INR 2.7 crore against INR 0.1 crore. FY26 revenue was INR 132.9 crore (up 40%), EBITDA INR 32.2 crore (24% margin) and PAT INR 5.3 crore. Management highlighted the TDR exchange mandate in Mumbai (BMC), an Airport Authority of India mandate, first CivitSUSTAIN order, and early German and US traction. Order book is about INR 232 crore against a pipeline of about INR 436 crore. This was the company's maiden earnings call.

segments.name: CivitPERMIT (flagship permitting)
segments.commentary: About 50% of FY26 revenue; management expects the same share in FY27, possibly higher due to transaction-based projects going live. Penetration cited at 1,500+ cities and 18 states.

segments.name: CivitINFRA
segments.commentary: About 25% of FY26 revenue; expected to be flat or slightly lower in FY27. Airport Authority of India order of INR 16-17 crore (incl. GST) is a one-time licence, with about 40% recognised in FY26 and the balance over about three years.

segments.name: CivitBUILD, BIM/GIS services and others
segments.commentary: Together about 15-20% of revenue. CivitBUILD has won private construction-enterprise projects; Middle East and African work exists.

segments.name: TDR exchange (Civit TDR)
segments.commentary: Transaction model earning 0.5% of TDR trade value, with Mumbai BMC transactions of about INR 8,000 crore in FY26 (implied about INR 40 crore revenue at 0.5%). Mandatory on the platform from 10 May 2026; management cites 70-80% margins. Revenue recognised in FY27 expected to be partial.

guidance_outlook: Target revenue of about INR 300 crore in three years (by FY29), with about 50% from India and rising overseas share.
EBITDA margin guided at a conservative 28-30%, potentially higher with overseas and TDR mix.
FY27 growth targeted at 25-27% (management also mentioned about 20% normal growth on ongoing business, with TDR upside), with a relatively conservative stance.
Management expects Germany commercial traction in about six months; Q3-Q4 FY27 cited for possible news, and US and Middle East targets for FY27.
Transaction-based revenue rose to INR 31-32 crore in FY26 from INR 20-23 crore in FY25 (about 40-45% growth).
capex_capacity: Intangibles (about INR 70 crore), intangibles under development (about INR 19 crore) and other financial assets (about INR 12 crore) were flagged by an analyst; management attributed these to capitalised product innovation, amortised over 3-4 years.
Company has about 550 staff, of which about 70% are in R&D, implementation and delivery; business development is about 25-30 people.
Germany: 100% subsidiary created via acquisition of a local company; German sales leader recruited and more hiring planned.
Germany prototyping with customers over the next three months, with a dual launch of the twinning platform and permitting portal planned.
CivitTwin AI platform (12 agents) launched in Mumbai; a German version has been launched.
demand_pricing: Order book approx. INR 232 crore; management says about 60% will convert to revenue in the year, roughly 40% of that recurring.
Pipeline of about INR 436 crore with management citing a conversion probability above 60% on bids where the company is engaged early; guided RFP win rate about 70%, losses mostly on price.
Oman tender: company is L2 on price and T1 on technology; the customer is seeking further price negotiation against a Singapore bidder, and war-related uncertainty is delaying the decision.
Government receivables are slow; management flagged a provision of about INR 2.5 crore, versus INR 45 lakh earlier, for retentions and deposits, recoverable over time.
Gratuity liability was increased by provisions tied to the revised Labour Code effective November 2025.

qa_highlights.question: Split of order book between transaction and project based, and conversion rate on pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book about INR 200-odd crore, about 60% to be booked this year, roughly 40% of that recurring. Pipeline conversion probability is above 60%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did provisions rise from INR 45 lakh to about INR 2.5 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Government retentions and deposits of 1-2% of invoice value are held for long periods. Provisions were taken per accounting standards for dues beyond about three years, and are expected to be recovered and reversed later. The gratuity provision reflects the revised Labour Code.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Airport Authority order be enhanced, and is it SaaS or one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR 16-17 crore order is a one-time licence. Phase one was completed and praised by the Civil Aviation Minister, with possible follow-on digital twin work.

qa_highlights.question: Details of the CivitSUSTAIN order with Mitsubishi and the GIFT City pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: First CivitSUSTAIN order came via Mitsubishi controllers used by L&T, for a Delhi Jal Board water-network digital twin. Formal announcement awaits Mitsubishi Japan approval. GIFT City is still awaiting a mandate.

qa_highlights.question: How many TDR registrations, and what is the revenue model?
qa_highlights.answer: About 100 registrations and some transactions so far. Revenue is 0.5% of TDR exchange transaction value. FY26 BMC volume was about INR 8,000 crore; MMRDA, MSRDC, Navi Mumbai, Vasai-Virar and Thane are additional and are being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 revenue reach about INR 170 crore including TDR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TDR revenue will not be fully recognised in FY27 because many transactions occurred before the mandate. Growth will come from TDR plus about 20% growth in existing businesses, with a 25-27% FY27 target.

qa_highlights.question: Germany and US: timing and revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Germany: prototyping over three months, commercial traction in about six months, with good news possible in Q3-Q4 FY27. US: smaller orders won, POCs done, a partner signed, and US revenue was recognised in FY26 though small.

qa_highlights.question: What is the defensibility against AI-driven replication, and how big is the team?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a 15-year permit dataset as a moat and the enterprise penetration as a barrier. Team growth will be slower than revenue growth, with some specialist hiring.

risks_watch: Government receivables and long collection cycles: DSO improved to 260 days, but provisions were raised and recovery is dependent on government processes.
Oman tender outcome, given the price gap against a Singapore bidder and war-related uncertainty.
TDR revenue concentration on a single municipality (BMC) and dependence on mandate enforcement since 10 May 2026.
US and German expansion remain unproven in revenue terms; management gave no firm quantum.
RFP-based revenue with price-led losses; the airport order is a one-time licence, so recurring revenue depends on AMC and new projects.
Intangible assets and capitalised development: amortisation over 3-4 years could weigh on margins.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, TDR and the Airport Authority win, but cautious on the Oman tender, US traction and government collections. Several answers were vague or deferred on specifics such as exact churn, the Germany revenue quantum, and the GIFT City mandate.
